# waveform-playlist

> Multitrack Web Audio editor and player with canvas waveform visualization. Two UI surfaces over a shared framework-agnostic engine: a React component library (`@waveform-playlist/browser`, Tone.js backend) and framework-agnostic Web Components (`@dawcore/components`, native Web Audio backend).

## What It Does

waveform-playlist builds browser-based audio editing applications. Use the React surface (`@waveform-playlist/browser`) or the framework-agnostic Web Components surface (`@dawcore/components`, `<daw-editor>` — works in any framework or vanilla HTML). Both provide:

- Multitrack audio playback, mixing, and editing
- Canvas-based waveform and spectrogram rendering with zoom
- Click-to-seek, drag-to-select, clip drag/trim/split
- Vertical track reordering via drag grip or move up/down buttons (undoable)
- 20 real-time audio effects (reverb, delay, EQ, compression, etc.) via Tone.js
- Time-synchronized annotations with drag editing
- Recording with live waveform preview and VU level metering (input and output)
- WAV export with offline rendering
- BBC audiowaveform support for instant rendering of large files
- Sample rate hint for pre-computed peaks matching (`sampleRate` prop on provider)
- Theming via styled-components

## Packages

- `@waveform-playlist/browser` — Main package: React components, hooks, effects. Playout engines (`@waveform-playlist/playout` + `tone`, or `@waveform-playlist/media-element-playout`) are optional peer dependencies; provide `createAdapter`/`createPlayout` to inject a custom engine.
- WAM 2.0 plugin hosting (from `@waveform-playlist/browser/tone`) — `addWamEffect`/`addWamEffectToTrack` host third-party [Web Audio Modules](https://www.webaudiomodules.com/) plugins alongside built-in Tone.js effects, requires native AudioContext mode (`configureGlobalContext({ nativeAudioContext: true })` from `@waveform-playlist/playout`; Firefox falls back automatically). `WamEffectGui` mounts plugin GUIs; `fetchWamLibrary`/`fetchWamDescriptor` from the optional `@dawcore/wam` peer discover community plugins. Same native-context call enables WAM hosting on `<daw-editor>`'s Tone.js backend (`createToneAdapter()`).
- `@waveform-playlist/core` — Data model: ClipTrack, AudioClip, sample-based math, `carveClipRange` (punch-in), `enumerateMicrophones`/`watchMicrophoneDevices` (permission-free device listing), `createPanStage`/`panMatrix` (the gain-matrix track pan stage every renderer uses instead of a `StereoPannerNode` or Tone `Panner` — pan law chosen by the track's source channel count, so a stereo effect on a mono track neither changes its level nor collapses to mono), the effect registry shared by `<daw-editor>` and the React effects hooks (`registerEffect(type, definition)`, `unregisterEffect`, `getEffectDefinitions`, `prepareEffect`, `ensureEffectPrepared`, `needsPrepare`, `createEffectInstance(type, audioContext, params)`; types `NativeEffectDefinition`, `NativeEffectInstance`, `EffectParamDef`, `CreatedNativeEffect` — one `registerEffect()` call makes a custom AudioWorklet or native-node effect available to both surfaces; the registry state lives on `globalThis`, so two installed copies of core share it)
- `@waveform-playlist/engine` — Framework-agnostic timeline engine: PlaylistEngine class, pure clip/timeline operations, event emitter. Owns selection, loop, zoom, volume, selectedTrackId, and clip mutation state. Seek/play beyond audio duration is supported (silence where there's no audio).
- `@waveform-playlist/playout` — Audio playback: Tone.js adapter (implements PlayoutAdapter from engine), global AudioContext. Peer `tone ^15.0.0`: stable (`npm install tone`, 15.1.x) is the default; the prerelease line (`npm install tone@next`, 15.5.x) is also supported and CI-tested, and is the one on which `configureGlobalContext({ sampleRate })` is honoured on the default (non-native) context. Incremental track updates via updateTrack/replaceClips — no full playout rebuild on clip operations. Optional adapter methods: addTrack, removeTrack, updateTrack.
- `@waveform-playlist/ui-components` — Styled primitives, theming, virtual scrolling contexts, playhead components, PlaylistErrorBoundary, BeatsAndBarsProvider
- `@waveform-playlist/annotations` — Annotation parsing, rendering, keyboard controls
- `@waveform-playlist/recording` — Microphone access, AudioWorklet recording, VU meter, integrated recording hook, mic-unplug detection
- `@waveform-playlist/worklets` — Shared AudioWorklet processors: `meter-processor` (sample-accurate peak/RMS metering) and `recording-processor` (multi-channel audio capture). Auto-installed with recording package.
- `@waveform-playlist/webaudio-peaks` — Peak extraction from AudioBuffer
- `@waveform-playlist/media-element-playout` — HTMLAudioElement playback with pitch-preserving speed control, optional Web Audio routing for fades and Tone.js effect bridging
- `@waveform-playlist/midi` — React layer for MIDI: `useMidiTracks` hook converts .mid files to ClipTrack[] with midiNotes for piano roll visualization and SoundFont/PolySynth playback. As of v13+ the parser is re-exported from `@dawcore/midi`; React API surface is unchanged. The SoundFont can be provided or swapped after setup via `adapter.setSoundFontCache()` on the adapter returned by `createToneAdapter()` (the React provider forwards late `soundFontCache` prop changes automatically; construct caches with `SoundFontCache.fromUrl(url)`).
- `@dawcore/components` — Web Components for multi-track audio editing (Lit-based). Elements: `<daw-editor>`, `<daw-track>`, `<daw-clip>`, `<daw-waveform>`, `<daw-playhead>`, `<daw-ruler>`, `<daw-selection>`, `<daw-track-controls>`, `<daw-grid>` (beats/bars grid), `<daw-piano-roll>` (MIDI), `<daw-spectrogram>` (per-track FFT via `render-mode="spectrogram"`), `<daw-transport>` + transport buttons (`<daw-play-button>`, `<daw-pause-button>`, `<daw-stop-button>`, `<daw-record-button>`), `<daw-time-display>`, `<daw-time-format>`, `<daw-keyboard-shortcuts>`, `<daw-annotation-track>` + `<daw-annotation>` (declarative annotation timeline lane — reflected `start`/`end`, drag boundary editing, `keyboard-controls` navigation) + `<daw-annotation-list for="trackId">` (linked text-panel dual view, same underlying data), and `<daw-player>` (lightweight single-track HTMLMediaElement player on `@waveform-playlist/media-element-playout` — no engine/adapter/AudioContext required). Framework-agnostic — works in any framework or vanilla HTML. No Tone.js dependency; uses native Web Audio via `@dawcore/transport`. Consumer supplies a `PlayoutAdapter` (no default). Unified effects chains: `addEffect`/`removeEffect`/`setEffectParams`/`setEffectBypassed`/`moveEffect`/`effects` on `<daw-track>` (per-track chain) and `<daw-editor>` (master chain), with built-in `native-*` effects (gain, compressor, stereo panner, delay, and one type per biquad filter shape: `native-filter` = lowpass, `native-highpass`, `native-bandpass`, `native-notch`, `native-peaking`, `native-lowshelf`, `native-highshelf`), custom registration via `registerEffect` from `@waveform-playlist/core` (`@dawcore/components` no longer exports `registerEffect`, `getEffectDefinitions`, `prepareEffect`, `createEffectInstance` or the definition types — import them from `@waveform-playlist/core`, where the types are `NativeEffectDefinition`, `NativeEffectInstance`, `EffectParamDef`; definitions may declare an async `prepare(audioContext)` hook for AudioWorklet-backed effects — awaited by `exportAudio()`/`setEffectsState()`; call `editor.prepareEffect(type)` before the synchronous `addEffect`), and `daw-effect-add/remove/change/bypass/reorder` events. WAM 2.0 plugins join the same chains via `addWamPlugin(url)` (optional `@dawcore/wam` peer); Faust DSP source compiles in the browser into the same chains via `addFaustEffect(dspCode, {name?})` (optional `@dawcore/faust` peer — entries persist as `{kind:'wam', faustDsp, faustName, state}` and recompile on restore/export; compile errors keep Faust's line/column diagnostics and leave the chain untouched). Effect GUIs: `openEffectGui(effectId, container)`/`closeEffectGui(effectId)` on both elements mount a WAM plugin's own GUI (or a generic parameter panel for GUI-less plugins and `native-*` effects) into a consumer-provided container — close hides without interrupting audio, the element is cached for reopen, and the GUI is destroyed only when the effect is removed. Persistence: `getEffectsState()`/`setEffectsState(entries)` on both elements serialize/restore chains (WAM entries carry the plugin's getState snapshot; an unreachable saved URL becomes a bypassed passthrough placeholder + `daw-effect-error`, restore continues). Offline export: `editor.exportAudio({sampleRate?, startTime?, duration?, channels?})` renders the session through all chains on an OfflineAudioContext (WAM plugins re-instantiated offline with saved state) and resolves to an AudioBuffer. Runnable WAM demo: `examples/dawcore-wam/` (`pnpm example:dawcore-wam`). Vertical track reordering: `<daw-editor track-reordering>` shows a drag grip + move up/down buttons on `<daw-track-controls>`; `editor.reorderTrack(trackId, toIndex)` moves programmatically. DOM order is the visual authority (moving a `<daw-track>` element syncs the engine); undoable.
- `@dawcore/midi` — Framework-agnostic MIDI parser (`parseMidiFile`, `parseMidiUrl` — pure functions, no React). Used by `@dawcore/components` via dynamic import inside `editor.loadMidi()`, and re-exported by `@waveform-playlist/midi`.
- `@waveform-playlist/spectrogram` — Optional spectrogram package (v13+): React `SpectrogramProvider` + UI (menu items, settings modal) integrating via `SpectrogramIntegrationContext`. Computation/worker/orchestrator are imported from `@dawcore/spectrogram`.
- `@dawcore/spectrogram` — Framework-agnostic FFT computation, Web Worker, and `SpectrogramOrchestrator` class (viewport classification, 3-tier render, generation-based abort, contiguous chunk grouping, color LUT cache). Shared between the React Provider and the dawcore Lit element layer.
- `@dawcore/transport` — Native Web Audio transport (no Tone.js; its only dependency is `@waveform-playlist/core`): scheduler, clock, tempo/meter map, metronome, loop, meter-aware `quantizeTick`, a Worker-driven timer (keeps scheduling in hidden tabs) and a per-tick `tick` event for consumers that must poll the playhead off rAF. Replaces Tone.js Transport for the dawcore stack. Implements the `PlayoutAdapter` interface from `@waveform-playlist/engine` via `NativePlayoutAdapter`. Exposes effects insertion hooks (`connectTrackEffects(trackId, input, output)` — a PRE-FADER track insert: clips → effects → volume → pan → mute — and `connectMasterOutput`) used by the dawcore effects chains. Track effects are pre-fader in every renderer (web components, React/Tone, and both offline exports): the fader never changes how hard a compressor works.
- `@dawcore/faust` — ONLY for live (in-browser) Faust compilation; for effects known at build time, precompile instead (guide: /docs/faust-effects — `faust2wasm` + `registerEffect` (from `@waveform-playlist/core`)/`prepare` for an AudioWorklet effect, loaded with `track.addEffect(id)` in web components or `addEffect(id)` in React, or `faust2wam` + `addWamPlugin(url)`/`addWamEffect(url)` for a WAM plugin; serve the compiled folder as static files, never through the bundler). Licences: `@dawcore/faust` is MIT but loads `@shren/faust2wam` (LGPL-3.0), whose bundle includes the faustwasm runtime (LGPL) and faust-ui (GPL-3.0-or-later); precompiled output still ships the LGPL faustwasm runtime, and `faust2wam` output includes faust-ui unless removed. In-browser Faust DSP compilation to WAM 2.0 plugins: `compileFaustToWam(dspCode, {name?})` wraps `@shren/faust2wam`'s generate() with a cached lazy compiler load (the ~2.5 MB gzipped libfaust WASM ships inside the dependency, loaded on first compile only). Returns `{factory, name, dspCode}` — the factory instantiates via `@dawcore/wam`'s `createWamInstanceFromFactory`. Faust compile errors propagate unchanged with line/column diagnostics. Optional peer of `@dawcore/components` — dynamic-imported by `addFaustEffect()`, so non-Faust users load zero compiler bytes.
- `@dawcore/wam` — Web Audio Modules (WAM 2.0) plugin hosting: idempotent host initialization (`ensureWamHost`), plugin loading/validation (`createWamInstance` from a URL or `createWamInstanceFromFactory` from an already-obtained WebAudioModule class, both with optional `createGui`/`destroyGui` passthroughs), library manifest discovery (`fetchWamLibrary` — webaudiomodules.com community registry and pedalboard2/wam-studio manifest shapes, `baseUrl` option for registry-relative paths), plain-DOM GUI helpers (`createParameterPanel`, `createWamParameterPanel` — generic slider panels from parameter metadata, themable via `--daw-*` CSS custom properties), transport sync (`createWamTransportBridge` — broadcasts `wam-transport` events with tempo/timeSig/bar/playing to plugin nodes on every transport event and, via the transport's Worker-driven `tick` event, on variable-tempo boundary crossings and loop wraps — no rAF, so plugins stay in sync in a hidden tab), and offline cloning (`cloneInstanceInto` — re-instantiates a plugin on an OfflineAudioContext with its getState snapshot, used by `exportAudio`). Optional peer of `@dawcore/components` — dynamic-imported by `addWamPlugin()`/`openEffectGui()`, so non-WAM users load zero WAM bytes.

## Requirements and Upgrading

- The React packages (`@waveform-playlist/browser`, `ui-components`, `annotations`, `spectrogram`, `recording`, `midi`) require `react` and `react-dom` `^19.0.0` and `styled-components` `^6.0.0`.
- Upgrading from an earlier major: follow https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/upgrading — it lists every breaking change with a Find / Replace-with entry, written so a coding agent can apply it mechanically.

## Quick Start

```tsx
import { WaveformPlaylistProvider, Waveform, PlayButton, PauseButton, StopButton } from '@waveform-playlist/browser';
import { useAudioTracks } from '@waveform-playlist/browser/tone';

function App() {
  const { tracks, loading } = useAudioTracks([
    { src: '/audio/track1.mp3', name: 'Track 1' },
    { src: '/audio/track2.mp3', name: 'Track 2' },
  ]);

  if (loading) return <div>Loading...</div>;

  return (
    <WaveformPlaylistProvider tracks={tracks} timescale controls={{ show: true, width: 200 }}>
      <PlayButton /> <PauseButton /> <StopButton />
      <Waveform />
    </WaveformPlaylistProvider>
  );
}
```

## Web Components Quick Start

No React and no build step — drop `<daw-editor>` into any HTML page and assign a `PlayoutAdapter`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@dawcore/components';
  import { NativePlayoutAdapter } from '@dawcore/transport';

  const editor = document.querySelector('daw-editor');
  editor.adapter = new NativePlayoutAdapter(new AudioContext());
</script>

<daw-editor id="editor" samples-per-pixel="1024" wave-height="100" timescale>
  <daw-track src="/audio/drums.opus" name="Drums"></daw-track>
  <daw-track src="/audio/bass.opus" name="Bass"></daw-track>
</daw-editor>

<daw-transport for="editor">
  <daw-play-button></daw-play-button>
  <daw-pause-button></daw-pause-button>
  <daw-stop-button></daw-stop-button>
</daw-transport>
```

`<daw-editor>` does not create an `AudioContext` — you own it and assign a `PlayoutAdapter`: `NativePlayoutAdapter` (from `@dawcore/transport`) for native Web Audio, or a Tone.js adapter (from `@waveform-playlist/playout`) when you need MIDI playback.

## Architecture

Both providers use React Context with split contexts for performance (7 in WaveformPlaylistProvider, 4 in MediaElementPlaylistProvider).

**WaveformPlaylistProvider** (multi-track, Web Audio API):
1. **usePlaybackAnimation()** — isPlaying, timing refs (currentTimeRef for the live position), per-frame callback registry (NOT currentTime)
2. **usePlaylistState()** — Medium-frequency: loop, annotations, selectedTrackId, settings (NOT the selection, NOT activeAnnotationId)
3. **useSelection()** — selectionStart, selectionEnd; changes on every pointer move of a selection drag
4. **useCurrentTime()** — currentTime: where the cursor rests; changes on seek, pause, stop and a leftward selection drag, does not advance during playback
5. **useActiveAnnotation()** — activeAnnotationId; changes at every annotation boundary during playback
6. **usePlaylistControls()** — Stable: play/pause/stop/seekTo, setSelection, track controls, zoom, settings setters, annotationPreview (a source: the annotations as an edge drag in progress would leave them)
7. **usePlaylistData()** — Stable: duration, tracks, trackStates, playoutRef (PlaylistEngine), isDraggingRef, display config, isReady

**MediaElementPlaylistProvider** (single-track, HTMLAudioElement):
1. **useMediaElementAnimation()** — isPlaying, currentTime
2. **useMediaElementState()** — continuousPlay, annotations, playbackRate
3. **useMediaElementControls()** — play/pause/stop/seekTo, setPlaybackRate, annotationPreview
4. **useMediaElementData()** — duration, peaksDataArray, sampleRate, display config

## Key Hooks

*From `@waveform-playlist/browser` (core, engine-free):*
- `useAnnotationDragHandlers(opts)` — Drag handlers for annotation box edges. Pass `preview: annotationPreview` (from `usePlaylistControls()` / `useMediaElementControls()`) and each move is published to the preview while `onAnnotationsChange` is called once, on release; without it, once per move. Escape restores every annotation the drag moved. `useAnnotationsWithPreview(annotations, annotationPreview)` returns what to draw in a custom annotation renderer.
- `useClipDragHandlers(opts)` — Drag-to-move and boundary trimming, delegates to engine.moveClip()/trimClip()
- `useDragSensors(opts?)` — Configures PointerSensor activation constraints for DragDropProvider (distance-based default, optional touch-optimized mode)
- `ClipCollisionModifier` — Collision detection modifier for clip moves, prevents overlapping clips
- `SnapToGridModifier` — Snap-to-grid modifier for clip moves. Two modes: `'beats'` (PPQN tick grid) and `'timescale'` (sample-based grid). Snaps absolute position, not delta.
- `useClipSplitting(opts)` — Split clips at playhead, delegates to engine.splitClip()
- `useKeyboardShortcuts(opts)` — Custom keyboard shortcuts
- `usePlaybackShortcuts(opts)` — Default playback shortcuts (Space, Escape, 0). Shortcuts never take a key the focused control uses, however it got focus: inputs (incl. sliders, checkboxes) and `<select>` keep all keys, Escape closes an open modal dialog, Space/Enter go to a focused `<button>` or `<summary>` (Enter only for a link) (after clicking Mute, Space toggles Mute; Space is play/pause when focus is not on a control)
- `useUndoState(opts)` — Undo/redo state (canUndo, canRedo, undo, redo) with engine delegation
- `KeyboardShortcuts` — Self-closing component for declarative keyboard shortcut setup. Props: `playback` (Space/Escape/0), `clipSplitting` ('s' key), `annotations` (arrow nav, boundary editing), `undo` (Cmd/Ctrl+Z, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z), `additionalShortcuts`. All booleans default to false. Reads all required data from context.

*From `@waveform-playlist/browser/tone` (Tone.js batteries-included):*
- `useAudioTracks(configs, options?)` — Load audio files into ClipTrack[] for the provider (declarative, configs-driven). Options: `{ immediate: true }` renders placeholder tracks instantly while audio decodes
- `useDynamicTracks()` — Imperative hook for runtime track additions (drag-and-drop, file picker). Creates placeholder tracks instantly while audio decodes in parallel
- `useDynamicEffects()` — Master effects chain with runtime add/remove/reorder/bypass/parameter updates. Returns `effects` (a `ValueSource<ActiveEffect[]>`, NOT an `activeEffects` array: read it with `useActiveEffects(effects)`), `availableEffects`, `addEffect(id): Promise<string>` (resolves with the instanceId; rejects for an unknown id), `addWamEffect(url)`, `removeEffect`, `updateParameter`, `toggleBypass`, `reorderEffects`, `clearAllEffects`, `masterEffects` (pass to the provider's `effects` prop), `createOfflineEffectsFunction()` (always returns a function, the same one on every call; it reads the chain when the export runs), `analyserRef`. The hook does not re-render when the chain changes and everything it returns is identity-stable. Call it ONCE and pass the result down (a second call creates a second, empty chain). `availableEffects` = the built-ins plus, only in native-context mode, registered custom types; it is read when the calling component renders (not subscribed), so register custom effects before the component that shows the picker renders. The chain survives a StrictMode remount, Fast Refresh and a hidden `<Activity>` (no cleanup on unmount): add defaults on mount behind a ref guard; instances of an unmounted chain are disposed when it is garbage-collected (best effort), or at a known moment by `clearAllEffects()`, which also rejects any add still in flight ("aborted: the effects chain was cleared")
- `useTrackDynamicEffects()` — Per-track effects management. Returns `getTrackEffects(trackId)` (a `ValueSource<TrackActiveEffect[]>` per track, NOT a `trackEffectsState` map: read it with `useActiveEffects(getTrackEffects(trackId))`), `addEffectToTrack(trackId, id): Promise<string>`, `addWamEffectToTrack`, `removeEffectFromTrack`, `updateTrackEffectParameter`, `toggleBypass(trackId, instanceId)`, `reorderTrackEffects(trackId, fromIndex, toIndex)`, `clearTrackEffects(trackId)` (disposes that track's effects and rejects its adds still in flight; chains are not disposed on unmount, same lifetime as the master chain), `getTrackEffectsFunction(trackId)` (same function per track id, never undefined; pass the function itself to the provider: `<WaveformPlaylistProvider trackEffects={getTrackEffectsFunction}>`. Tracks have no `effects` field: never copy track objects to attach effects), `createOfflineTrackEffectsFunction(trackId)` (never undefined), `availableEffects`
- `useActiveEffects(source)` — Subscribes a component to one effects chain and returns `ActiveEffect[]`. Call it in the component that draws the rack, not at the page root; that component re-renders when the chain changes
- Custom effects in React — register an AudioWorklet or native-node effect with `registerEffect(id, definition)` from `@waveform-playlist/core` (definition: `label`, `category`, `defaults`, `params`, `create(audioContext, params)`, optional async `prepare(audioContext)` and `wetParam`), then `addEffect(id)` / `addEffectToTrack(trackId, id)`. Requires native-context mode (`configureGlobalContext({ nativeAudioContext: true })` from `@waveform-playlist/playout` before any audio initialization, as for WAM; otherwise the add rejects). `prepare` is awaited by `addEffect` on the live context and by WAV export on the offline context. Parameters are numeric (`updateParameter` ignores a non-number for a custom effect). The host owns every connection out of the instance's `output` and disconnects all of them on a rewire: do not connect `output` to anything inside the effect. An AudioWorklet effect's `dispose` should tell the processor to stop over its port (do not return `false` from `process()` while the effect may be reconnected: a bypassed-by-disconnection processor did not restart in Chrome). If the chain cannot be rewired with the new effect, the previous chain is restored and the add rejects. Bypass zeroes `wetParam` when the definition has one, otherwise disconnects the effect. Entries have `kind: 'custom'` (`ActiveEffect.kind` is `'tone' | 'wam' | 'custom'`; `'tone'` = built-in Tone.js effect, called `'native'` before the next major; `<daw-editor>`'s own `kind: 'native'` is a different type and unchanged). Guide: /docs/react/guides/effects#custom-effects `availableEffects` lists the Tone.js effects and the app's own registered types; `@dawcore/components`' `native-*` effects (marked `builtIn` in the shared registry) are left out of it but can be added by id.
- `useExportWav()` — Offline WAV export with effects support
- `useOutputMeter(options?)` — Real-time master output VU meter. Returns `{ meter, resetPeak, error }`; `meter` is a `MeterSource` (`subscribe` / `getSnapshot` over `{ levels, peakLevels, rmsLevels }`), not state, so the hook does not re-render as levels change. Draw it with `<SegmentedVUMeter meter={meter} />`
- `useMasterAnalyser(fftSize?)` — FFT analyser wired in parallel to the master output. Returns `{ analyserRef, masterEffects }` — pass `masterEffects` to the provider's `effects` prop and read frequency data from `analyserRef.current`
- `ExportWavButton` — Pre-built button component wired to useExportWav
- `effectDefinitions`, `effectCategories`, `getEffectDefinition`, `getEffectsByCategory`, `createEffectInstance(definition, initialParams?)`, `createEffectChain` — Factory and definitions for the built-in Tone.js effects. An `EffectInstance` has `input` and `output` nodes (not `effect`). `getAvailableEffects()` lists the built-ins followed, in native-context mode only, by registered custom types (a read, not a subscription); `createCustomEffectInstance(type, audioContext, params?)` builds a registered one. The registry itself (`registerEffect`, …) is in `@waveform-playlist/core`

### MIDI Hooks (from `@waveform-playlist/midi`)

- `useMidiTracks(configs, options)` — Load .mid files into ClipTrack[] with midiNotes for piano roll rendering. `options: { sampleRate: number }`. One config can produce multiple tracks (one per MIDI channel). Supports pre-parsed notes via `midiNotes` prop. `configs` is compared by value, so an inline array literal is fine; files load in parallel and tracks keep config order.
- `parseMidiFile(data, options?)` — Pure function: ArrayBuffer → ParsedMidi with tracks, notes, tempo, time signature. No React dependency. Re-exported from `@dawcore/midi`.
- `parseMidiUrl(url, options?, signal?)` — Fetch + parse convenience wrapper with AbortSignal support. Re-exported from `@dawcore/midi`.

### MIDI Loading (from `@dawcore/components`, requires optional `@dawcore/midi` peer dep)

- `editor.loadMidi(source, options?)` — Imperatively load a `.mid` file (URL string or File) and create N `<daw-track>` elements with `render-mode="piano-roll"` — one per note-bearing MIDI track. Returns `Promise<MidiLoadResult>` with `{ trackIds, bpm, timeSignature, duration, name }`. Cleanup-on-failure via `Promise.allSettled`: any per-track failure removes every track appended during the call. Dynamic-imports `@dawcore/midi` on first call; throws friendly install hint if missing.
- `MidiLoadOptions` — `{ startTime?: number; signal?: AbortSignal }`. `signal` is forwarded to `fetch()` only; aborting after parse is a no-op.
- `MidiLoadResult` — `{ readonly trackIds: readonly string[]; readonly bpm: number; readonly timeSignature: readonly [number, number]; readonly duration: number; readonly name: string }`.

### Beats & Bars (from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`)

- `BeatsAndBarsProvider` — Optional context providing BPM, time signature, and snap config. Wraps playlist content to enable beats & bars timescale mode in SmartScale. Props: `bpm`, `timeSignature: [number, number]`, `snapTo: 'bar' | 'beat' | 'off'`
- `getScaleInfo(samplesPerPixel)` — Returns `{ marker, bigStep, smallStep }` (ms) for temporal timescale tick spacing at the given zoom level. Also useful for deriving `gridSamples` for `SnapToGridModifier` temporal mode.

### Virtual Scrolling Hooks (from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`)

- `useScrollViewport()` — Current scroll position and viewport dimensions (with 1.5x overscan buffer)
- `useVisibleChunkIndices(totalWidth, chunkWidth, originX?)` — Memoized array of visible chunk indices for canvas virtualization
- `useClipViewportOrigin()` — Clip's pixel offset in the timeline (for correct chunk visibility in multi-clip tracks)

### Recording Hooks (from `@waveform-playlist/recording`)

- `useIntegratedRecording(tracks, setTracks, selectedTrackId, options)` — Combined recording + track management: mic access, VU meter (`meter`, a `MeterSource`), live take progress (`progress`, a `RecordingProgressSource` to pass as `<Waveform recordingState={{ isRecording: true, trackId, startSample, progress, bits: 16 }} />`), start/stop/pause recording, adds the take at the record-start playhead position with punch-in replace semantics (overlapped clip content is trimmed/removed/split); recording latency compensation is configurable via `latencyOffset` (seconds) on both the React `IntegratedRecordingOptions` and the dawcore `RecordingOptions` passed to `editor.startRecording()`. `startRecording()` resolves `true` when capture actually started. For overdub, call `usePlaylistControls().setRecordingActive(true, trackId)` before `play()` — while the session is active the end-of-timeline auto-stop is suppressed (the take can run past existing audio) and the recorded-over track's existing content is transiently muted (punch-in replaces it); both reset automatically when the recording ends. `<daw-editor>` does both automatically during recording (no API call needed)
- `useRecording(stream, options)` — Low-level recording via AudioWorklet; `startRecording()` resolves `true`/`false` for capture start success. Elapsed time and live peaks come through `progress`, a `RecordingProgressSource` (`subscribe` / `getSnapshot` over `{ duration, peaks }`), not state
- `useRecordingProgress(progress, { updateRate? })` — A recording's `{ duration, peaks }` as React state, at most `updateRate` times a second (default 10); for an elapsed-time label
- `enumerateMicrophones()` / `watchMicrophoneDevices(listener)` — framework-agnostic, permission-free mic listing from `@waveform-playlist/core` (`hasLabels` false pre-permission: browsers redact labels)
- `useMicrophoneAccess()` — Request mic permission, enumerate devices, get MediaStream
- `useMicrophoneLevel(stream, options?)` — Real-time VU meter levels from mic stream (supports multi-channel via `channelCount` option). Returns `{ meter, resetPeak, error }`; `meter` is a `MeterSource`, not state
- `useOutputMeter(options?)` — Real-time master output VU meter (from `@waveform-playlist/browser/tone`). Returns `{ meter, resetPeak, error }`
- `useMeterLevels(meter, { updateRate? })` (from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`) — A meter's `{ levels, peakLevels, rmsLevels }` as React state, at most `updateRate` times a second (default 10). `useThrottledValue(source, options?)` is the generic form for any `ValueSource`
- `SegmentedVUMeter` (from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`) — LED-style meter. `meter={meter}` draws a live `MeterSource` directly to the DOM without re-rendering; `levels` / `peakLevels` props remain for values you hold yourself
- Meter levels and recording progress change ~60 times a second, so these hooks return a source (`ValueSource<T>` from `@waveform-playlist/core`: `subscribe(listener)` + `getSnapshot()`, compatible with `useSyncExternalStore`) instead of state. Migration from the old `levels` / `duration` / `recordingPeaks` fields: https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/upgrading

## Key Components

- `WaveformPlaylistProvider` — Multi-track provider (Web Audio API / Tone.js). **Single instance per page** (shared Tone.js Transport). Props: tracks, timescale, controls, theme, effects, annotationList, onAnnotationsChange, onTracksChange, onReady, barWidth, barGap, roundedBars, waveHeight, samplesPerPixel, zoomLevels, mono
- `MediaElementPlaylistProvider` — Single-track provider (HTMLAudioElement). Multiple instances per page OK (independent audio elements). Props: track, audioContext, playbackRate, timescale, controls, theme, annotationList, onAnnotationsChange, onReady, barWidth, barGap, roundedBars, waveHeight, samplesPerPixel. Track config supports fadeIn/fadeOut (requires audioContext). Use for language learning, podcasts, single-track viewers, and Tone.js effect bridging.
- `Waveform` — Main visualization. Props: showClipHeaders, gainScaledWaveforms (draw each clip's waveform scaled by its gain; web-component equivalent: `<daw-editor gain-scaled-waveforms>`), interactiveClips, renderPlayhead, renderTrackControls, showFades, touchOptimized, trackReordering (drag grip + move up/down buttons on the default track control panel; drag requires ClipInteractionProvider, buttons work regardless)
- `SortableTrackControls` — Registers a custom track-controls row as a vertical drag source for `trackReordering`; exposes `ref`/`handleRef`/`isDragSource` render props. For consumers who don't use the default track control panel.
- `ClipInteractionProvider` — Declarative wrapper for clip drag/move/trim/snap/collision. Props: snap (boolean, auto-detects beats vs timescale from BeatsAndBarsProvider context), touchOptimized. Auto-enables interactiveClips on descendant Waveform. Replaces manual DragDropProvider + useClipDragHandlers + modifier setup. `useClipInteractionEnabled()` hook returns true when inside this provider.
- `KeyboardShortcuts` — Self-closing component for declarative keyboard shortcut setup. Props: `playback`, `clipSplitting`, `annotations`, `undo`, `additionalShortcuts`. All booleans default to false. Must be inside WaveformPlaylistProvider.
- Buttons (from `@waveform-playlist/browser`): PlayButton, PauseButton, StopButton, RewindButton, FastForwardButton, LoopButton, SetLoopRegionButton, ClearAllButton, ZoomInButton, ZoomOutButton
- Buttons (from `@waveform-playlist/browser/tone`): ExportWavButton
- Controls: MasterVolumeControl, TimeFormatSelect, AudioPosition, SelectionTimeInputs, AutomaticScrollCheckbox, ContinuousPlayCheckbox
